chapter: The jazz war with Leonard Feather
title: Back in New York: still working at trad places
summary: Hodes says the trouble did not run him out of town. He worked at Ryan's and the Vanguard, and Nick and Condon gave him some jobs.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, let's go back to your --

Well, I'm back to New York. All this is a New York happening. There's an involvement, there's a life there, it's alive. Even getting into all this trouble was an alive thing. It did not run me out of the business, didn't run me out of town. I was still able to find some --
Do you think that it helped you some? In getting work from the so-called moldy fig side of things?

Well, they were in my corner, anyway, whatever work -- and I was a promoter. If I'd never made it in music, I probably would have gone in for promo. I like to see something happening from nothing. I'm very attracted to that.

So but I wasn't going to lay down and die. I'd find something to do. And there were still trad places tha were going to run trad music. Jimmy Ryan's was still going to run, the Vanguard still used trad music, in spite of it. And there was outlying places. So I was able to work. And Nick gave me a few jobs here and there, not steady, because he had his favorites. I just wasn't one of his favorites. The

same with Condon. I was about fifth on his list. But that's got nothing to do with it. He was fifth on my list of guitar players. This is a thing that a person should be allowed to have, his favorites. If I talk to you about your favorite clarinet player and if I was a clarinet player I might be sixth.
